deliverables.title: P1 consistency rows: param totals from dims vs published, <= 7B (lands with P1)
deliverables.report: llm_util.model_raw_param_count() is a block-aware raw-parameter census (embeddings, attention/MLA, Mamba1/Mamba2, gated DeltaNet, short conv, FFN/MoE, depth-shared groups counted once plus their LoRA). tests/test_qif_model_matrix.py asserts every YAML's census is within 3% of the published figure recorded in its provenance block (every row lands within 0.03% except minicpm3_4b at 1.84% and qwen3_5_4b at 5.14%) and that the census agrees with the row's d2_status against the 7B cutoff both ways. WAVE D: the per-row published_total_params_tolerance was uncapped and unexplained - it is now capped at 15% (past that the check stops distinguishing 'the published figure counts more than this YAML models' from 'the census is wrong'), may not be tighter than the 3% default, and above the default requires a published_total_params_tolerance_reason field, which qwen3_5_4b (0.06, rounded card figure plus vision tower and MTP head) and gemma_3_4b (0.10, the unmodeled 0.420B SigLIP tower) now carry. ASSUMPTION: three nominal-'7B' rows are over the D2 raw cutoff and are recorded as d2_status: reference following the ADJ-2 precedent (RWKV-7 7.2B, LFM2.5-8B) rather than dropped - falcon_h1_7b 7.585B, falcon_mamba_7b 7.271B, hunyuan_7b 7.504B raw params.

deliverables.title: P2 degenerate-reduction gates: slicing off / one owner reproduces today bit-identically (lands with P2)
deliverables.report: Two gates in tests/test_fws_cim.py, parametrized over fws_cim_optima_t1 + vit_huge_story_64, fws_cim_llama7b + llama2_7b_fws_inf, and fws_cim_moe + moe_small_fws_inf. The first runs run_perf twice per pair - shipped config, then the same config with an EXPLICIT but inert cim.cards (slicing off, bank = full mux depth) and cim.allocation (column_sets_per_tile = adc_mux) block - and asserts fws_cim_report.json and LLM_inference_results.txt are byte-identical; WAVE D routes both runs through a per-test --output_dir, so a second pytest session in the same checkout can no longer overwrite the very bytes this gate compares. The second compares the same pair at law level (vec_cycles, arrays, area, chip usage, every stage time, period, stack energy) and checks the tiled path reproduces analog_gemm_time per stage. ASSUMPTION: byte-identity of the two report artifacts is the operative definition of 'reproduces today's numbers bit-identically' for the full report output.

deliverables.title: Bridge gate: closed-form vs DAG on ViT tiers + Llama7b + MoE smoke at 1e-3 (ADJ-8; needs P4)
deliverables.report: fws_bridge projects the priced DAG onto the closed form's stage vocabulary and validate_fws_cim_vs_optima.py appends 231 bridge rows to the original 152: every discrete quantity exact, every continuous one at REL_TOL = 1e-3 (ADJ-8), with the closed form supplied by a run_perf SUBPROCESS from the same two YAMLs so nothing is self-referential. Nine exclusions are named and printed under the table. WAVE B FIX: a KV-read-bound decode attention stage used to emit ok=False and turn the whole validator red on a legitimate configuration; it is now the named kv_read_bound_decode exclusion, because the gate must go red on DISAGREEMENT and not on inapplicability, and no shipped bridge point hits it today. ASSUMPTION: on disagreement the DAG wins and the closed form carries the annotation; the closed form itself is frozen and unmodified (git diff shows zero changes to any report key).

deliverables.title: Standing suites stay green through every wave (123 fws_cim tests, 152-check validator, 221 goldens, A100 baselines)
deliverables.report: All three suites re-run serially at the end of the wave, with the pre-change baseline recorded first on the same tree. D2's own deltas: tests/test_fws_cim.py 199 -> 202, +25 tests (16 model-matrix, 4 mapping, 3 fws_cim, 2 atlas) and 0 validator rows. THE TREE AT CLOSE, which is what a rerun sees, is shared with builder D1's P3.7 and with the Wave D audit-fix pass: tests/test_fws_cim.py 202 passed; the validator ALL CHECKS PASS 423/423, exit 0 (383 + D1's 40 P3.7 rows); the full suite 2264 passed / 44 skipped / 7 xfailed / 2 xpassed / 0 failed, exit 0, 549 s serially (2229 D2 + 27 D1 + 8 audit-fix). The 221 golden-equivalence specs and both A100 bit-identity baselines sit inside that run and are unmoved. WAVE D: the shared-output race three auditors flagged is closed at the source - run_perf.py gained --output_dir and every test that drives run_perf writes into a per-test temp root, so two pytest sessions in one checkout can no longer overwrite each other's artifacts mid-assertion; ABSENT is byte-identical to BEFORE THE CHANGE, verified by running `git show HEAD:run_perf.py` from a scratch cwd and diffing its artifacts against an ordinary run of the current file (clean on fws_cim_optima_t1 + vit_huge_story_64 and on fws_cim_llama7b_mapped + llama2_7b_fws_inf; the flagged run diffs clean against both). AUDIT FIX: test_run_perf_gpu_results_unchanged_vs_baseline asserted that no CIM report exists after a GPU run, which the per-test root made VACUOUS (an empty tmp dir passes it whatever run_perf does); it now seeds a stale fws_cim_report.json into the root first, so the assertion again proves run_perf RECREATES exp_dir. DISCLOSED: tests/test_webui_browser.py stays a known full-suite intermittent (it passed in-suite on all Wave D runs, including this one).
